question_text: One hour after being admitted to the hospital for sharp, acute chest pain and diaphoresis, a 55-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus loses consciousness in the emergency department. There are no palpable pulses. Chest compressions are started. The patient has a history of breast cancer that was surgically treated 4 years ago. Prior to admission, the patient was on a long bus ride to visit her sister. Her medications include tamoxifen, atorvastatin, metoprolol, metformin, and insulin. Serum troponin levels are elevated. The cardiac rhythm is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
